gaps.note: Edit after the model leaves the stage.
Edit before Barbara asks about the founder's background.
Edit before Daymond begins his exit.

stage_a.note: The founder delivers the pitch with strong, confident energy and clear positive engagement.
Sustained excitement about internet culture and the game's mechanics is evident throughout.
Friendly and approachable demeanor, though primarily focused on delivering the pitch material.

venture.description: A board game parodying internet influencer culture where players compete to gain the most followers.
venture.note: The founder is seeking $500,000 for a 10% equity stake.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 delivers the prepared presentation, introducing the board game, its rules, and the initial investment ask.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks if F1 is going to demonstrate how the game works.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 agrees to show how to play and playfully dismisses the model from the stage.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks how many followers the model has on social media.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 deflects the question about the model and explains his own large following on social media.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks F1 to explain his own social media presence since she does not follow him.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 describes his social media accounts and the type of good news content he posts online.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 expresses his appreciation for the show and the investors, noting he has been a long-time viewer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks to return to the business at hand and explain the game mechanics.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains the board layout, the playing pieces, and how players move around and interact with spaces.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 reads a game card she drew from the box.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 reads a game card he drew, detailing a scenario.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks to confirm that the player with the most followers at the end of the game wins.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms that having the most followers is how the game is won.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 reads a game card she drew from the deck.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks F1 how he got involved in creating the board game.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains his background in comedy and sales, and his desire to create a physical product outside of algorithms.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks to hear about the business side of the venture.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 mentions they signed an exclusive deal with a major big box retailer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks how retail customers will know what the game is and be motivated to buy it.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 discusses their strategy, comparing it to another popular game and explaining their target demographic shift.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks for the total number of units sold.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states they have sold fifteen hundred units so far.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 states that the sales numbers are very poor.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks how many retail locations the game is currently in.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks to confirm the number of retail locations.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms the number of retail locations.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 argues the sales are too low for the number of locations and they will be delisted.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 defends the business, stating it has only been two months and the margins are good.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks for the specific financial numbers and costs.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 provides the manufacturing cost per unit.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks for the wholesale price.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 provides the retail, wholesale, and broker pricing details.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks for the direct to consumer sales figures.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states they have not made any direct to consumer sales.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks for the total dollar amount of product sold.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 provides the total dollar amount sold by the broker.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 expresses confidence that the games will eventually sell.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks if there is any other information to justify the high valuation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 admits that the valuation number was made up and is not based on current financials.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 exits, stating the valuation is insane given the current sales numbers.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 exits, citing the difficulty of the toy industry and the excessive valuation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 asks the remaining investors why they do not believe the company is worth the valuation.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 states it is because the company is not currently making money.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 concedes that they are not making money yet.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 points out that F1 is asking them to invest based only on future potential.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 notes the uncertainty of sales and says a smaller ask might have worked.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains he needed a larger amount to fulfill potential purchase orders from major retailers.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 explains the financial returns required to justify a five hundred thousand dollar investment.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 acknowledges the reality of their money and their desire to get it back.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 clarifies that investors expect a ten times return, reiterating the valuation was too high.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 exits, stating she likes social media but the investment is too risky.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 exits, noting the valuation is too rich compared to what game developers would charge.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 thanks the investor for their time.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 exits, praising F1's quick wit but stating the financial risk is too high.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 thanks the panel.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 suggests F1 use his social media handle on the game box.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 jokes about making a deal based on that advice.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 agrees the advice is good.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 jokingly asks if they have a deal.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 laughs and says he has a better chance with that strategy.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 wishes F1 good luck.

decisions.note: Numbers are insane, valuation is too high based on sales.
Toy industry is too hard, asked for too much money.
No idea if people will enjoy the game, too much money to risk.
Valuation is too rich, game developers could acquire a majority for that amount.
Asking too much money to risk on a chance.

record.notes: The model Chloe appears early on to pose but does not speak.
